gen-gf-jim-nightshade-manrope: Jim Nightshade scrawls like a pen left running, its close-set letters knitting into a dark, inky texture. Manrope follows in a plain sans, bright and open, and not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-montserrat: Montserrat brings wide, generous curves that glide under the eye, set against Jim Nightshade's smudgy, pen-scribbled headings. Expect it to wear thin over a long passage, since the heading's casual hand is happiest in small bursts.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-satoshi: Loose scribble up top, tall tidy letters below. Jim Nightshade is best at casual, ink-dark headings, while Satoshi's soaring x-height and open e do better with brief copy.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-switzer: Scribbled and crisp in one go: Jim Nightshade's pen-and-paper letters crowd together, while Switzer's wire-like sans keeps every c tip clear. And a handful of lines is where the two get along best.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-work-sans: Work Sans sits high and modern beneath the scrawl. Its c tips never creep toward touching, which gives Jim Nightshade's smudgy, close-packed pen strokes a crisp counterweight, though the pair suits short stretches of reading.
gen-gf-joti-one-fs-paquito: Joti One stamps out round, chunky letters with big-eyed e shapes and no stroke contrast at all. And Paquito's serif body keeps lowercase close to the capitals, friendly enough for a handful of lines.
gen-gf-julee-archivo: Archivo has a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, which makes Julee's cramped, cable-thick handwriting look even more hand-drawn. And that tension is the strongest thing here, though not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-julee-fs-asap: Julee presses small, thick letters tightly together with a rounded-nib look and no brush swell anywhere. And Asap answers in a sans-serif with open arcs and near-capital height, but it's not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-julee-fs-epilogue: Julee's friendly handwriting is packed tight like bundled cable. Epilogue loosens everything up in a sans-serif with curvy, unclamped letters, stubby ascenders and a wire-like skeleton, though not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-julee-fs-erode: Julee writes with a firm, rounded nib and no brush-style swelling, its small letters packed tight. Erode answers in a serif with a tall middle band and a faint ebb and flow of pressure, good for a handful of lines.
